steps.label: What they are, and their origin
steps.why: Microglia are the odd ones out among the supporting cells of the nervous system, because every other one comes from ectoderm, so the origin is the fact worth stating.
common_mistakes: Calling microglia neurons. They are supporting cells and carry no impulse.
Writing that they are ectodermal. Microglia are mesodermal in origin.
steps.memory_tip: All neuroglia are ectodermal except microglia, which come from mesoderm.
steps.margin_note: What they are, then where they come from. Two short lines.

steps.label: Their function
steps.why: A phagocytic cell of mesodermal origin is the defence cell of its tissue, and that is exactly the job microglia do inside the brain and spinal cord.
common_mistakes: Writing that they make myelin. Myelin is made by oligodendrocytes and by Schwann cells.
steps.memory_tip: Mesodermal origin and phagocytic job go together — both are unusual for a nerve tissue cell.
steps.margin_note: One word carries this mark — phagocytic. Say what they engulf.

lines.text: Phagocytic: they clear microbes and dead cells
